newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. anti-drug chief backs Panama drug center.
newsitem.headline: U.S. anti-drug chief backs Panama drug center.

text.p: U.S. anti-drug chief Barry McCaffrey on Monday backed a proposal to turn a U.S. military base in Panama into an international centre to fight drug trafficking.

"The Panamanian government's concept of an anti-drug centre is what I find attractive and it deserve serious study," the retired Army general told a news conference at the end of a three-day visit to review Panama's drug fighting initiatives.
"I think there is widespread agreement of all international partners that we must work together to fight drug trafficking," he added.

McCaffrey, former commander-in-chief of the United States Southern Command based in Panama, met Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares to discuss Panama's offer to allow the United States to keep strategic Howard Air Force Base at no cost for use as an international drug fighting centre.
"In my view we can't protect the region against drugs if we don't cooperate," McCaffrey said. He was to leave later on Monday for Peru.
